title: Apply Bitwise Operations to Make Strings Equal
summary: Given two binary strings s and target of the same length, you can perform an operation by choosing two distinct indices i and j (where 0 ≤ i, j < n ).
statement: Given two binary strings s and target of the same length, you can perform an operation by choosing two distinct indices i and j (where 0 ≤ i, j < n ). In this operation, simultaneously replace s[i] with (s[i] OR s[j]) and s[j] with (s[i] XOR s[j]) . For example, if s = "0110" , choosing i = 0 and j = 2 results in s[0] becoming 1 (since 0 OR 1 = 1 ) and s[2] becoming 1 (since 0 XOR 1 = 1 ), thus transforming s to "1110". Determine whether it is possible to transform s into target .
constraints: The equal-length strings contain only zero and one.
An operation replaces bits i,j simultaneously by their OR and XOR values.
Return whether any sequence of operations transforms s into target.
reference_solution:
def can_make_binary_strings_equal(s,target):
    return ('1' in s)==('1' in target)
hints: Study the operation on pairs 00, 01, 10, and 11.
An all-zero string remains all zero, while a string containing one can never lose its final one.
With at least one one, the allowed pair transformations can arrange any desired nonzero binary state.
Therefore reachability depends only on whether both strings contain at least one one or both contain none.
editorial: Therefore reachability depends only on whether both strings contain at least one one or both contain none.

tests.explanation: Both strings contain a one, and operations can reposition and change the count of ones.
An operation can never eliminate the final remaining one, so all-zero target is unreachable.
